title: Sensex Falls More Than 1,100 Points as Profit Booking Ends Rally's Winning Streak
excerpt: Investors lost over Rs 5.33 lakh crore in Monday's intraday sell-off, as a weaker rupee, US rate-hike expectations and heavyweight selling compounded profit booking after a record run.
body:
• The BSE Sensex was down 1,159 points, or 1.38%, at 82,760.74 at 1:27 p.m. IST on Monday, November 23, and the Nifty 50 was down 351 points, or 1.36%, at 25,449.90, according to The Times of India.
  • The sell-off wiped out over Rs 5.33 lakh crore of investor wealth, taking the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 509 lakh crore.
  • Reporting on the fall points to four drivers: profit booking after a record rally, revived expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike in December, a weaker rupee, and selling in heavyweight banking and financial stocks.
  • For NRI investors, the levels still sit near records: the Nifty is just over 2% below its lifetime high of 26,373.20, and the Sensex less than 3% below its record peak of 86,159.

Indian benchmark indices fell sharply on Monday, November 23, snapping a winning streak in the middle of a record rally. At 1:27 p.m. IST, the BSE Sensex was trading at 82,760.74, down 1,159 points or 1.38 per cent, and the Nifty 50 was at 25,449.90, down 351 points or 1.36 per cent, according to The Times of India. The Hindu businessline's live market coverage showed the slide deepening later in the session, with the Sensex down 1,169.73 points at 82,749.98 and the Nifty down 365.95 points at 25,434.65 on its market ticker.

The fall wiped out over Rs 5.33 lakh crore of investor wealth, with the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies dropping to Rs 509 lakh crore. Weakness spread beyond the benchmarks: the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices also slipped into negative territory, and businessline reported 2,692 stocks declining on the BSE against 1,547 advancing in the mid-session reversal. Banking stocks bore the brunt of the selling, while IT stocks bucked the trend — TCS, Tech Mahindra, Infosys and HCL Tech were among the Sensex stocks trading higher, along with Maruti Suzuki.

Why the market fell

Profit booking after a sharp rally. The Times of India identified profit booking as the biggest reason: the Nifty has gained more than 10 per cent in November and is on course for its best monthly performance since 2020, prompting investors to lock in gains. Indian equities had been approaching their previous record highs, supported by a turnaround in foreign institutional investor flows.

US rate-hike concerns. Expectations of tighter US monetary policy returned to the forefront, with markets assigning a 93 per cent probability to an interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting, according to CME's FedWatch tool as cited by The Times of India. On Friday, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook supported further rate increases, arguing the prevailing policy rate was not high enough to tackle inflation. A US rate increase can make American investments more attractive relative to Indian equities.

A weaker rupee. The rupee weakened sharply and was heading towards the 93-per-dollar level after briefly moving above 92.50, having closed at 92.67 on Friday. A weaker rupee raises the domestic cost of imports, particularly crude oil, and can erode the dollar-denominated returns earned by overseas investors, potentially prompting further foreign selling.

Heavyweight selling. Several of the market's biggest constituents — HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and Axis Bank — declined by as much as 2.5 per cent, and among Sensex constituents Tata Steel, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI and UltraTech Cement dropped by as much as 6 per cent. Because the indices are weighted by market capitalisation, falls in the heavyweights drag the benchmarks disproportionately.

"We are witnessing heightened volatility across markets — equity, currency and metals."

— VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments, to The Times of India

What to watch

Vijayakumar told The Times of India that India has been the best-performing large market in the world so far this month, helped by the change in the foreign-investor stance towards India and better-than-expected earnings growth, and he advised investors to manage the volatility with calm, systematic investing. The immediate tests are the Federal Reserve's December meeting, where markets currently price a high probability of a hike, and whether foreign flows hold after Monday's reversal. Monday's levels, it is worth noting, came after a steep climb: the Nifty is just over 2 per cent below its lifetime high of 26,373.20, and the Sensex less than 3 per cent below its record peak of 86,159.
